g.text: Proven Spring Boot architectures that safely decouple background tasks, preserve ACID transaction boundaries, and eliminate entity detachment traps.

text.tspan: // TX1 commits here before async dispatch

g.text: Main thread finishes & commits TX1 before email task starts.
Passing primitive Long orderId prevents LazyInitializationException.
Email timeouts or SMTP errors cannot rollback the committed order.
Worker holds no JDBC connection, saving database pool slots.
Order confirmation emails, SMS alerts, push notifications, webhooks, CDN purge.
Always invoke async method AFTER transactional method returns,
or use Spring's @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT) for strict ordering.
Worker Opens Autonomous TX2 (Async DB Writes)
// ASYNC WORKER SERVICE WITH INDEPENDENT DB TX
// 1. Fetch fresh entity in worker's own TX2 session:
// 2. Write audit record & commit TX2 independently:
// TX2 commits here autonomously. TX1 is unaffected!
REQUIRES_NEW instructs Spring to open fresh DB connection & TX2.
Reloading by ID ensures fresh entity state inside TX2's Hibernate session.
If audit logging throws exception, main order in TX1 stays committed.
Caller should commit TX1 before TX2 fires so findById() can read it.
Audit compliance trails, security event tracking, asynchronous billing telemetry.
Watch HikariCP database pool limits! Each active
REQUIRES_NEW worker holds an independent DB connection until completion.
// Await async result non-blockingly or join when ready:
Main thread and background worker execute CPU & IO concurrently.
Disables Hibernate dirty-checking, reduces memory and DB lock times.
Worker exceptions are safely captured inside the Future and caught on .join().
Returns collections or DTOs cleanly across threads without session leak.
Heavy analytical queries, dashboard aggregation, parallel microservice lookups.
Use CompletableFuture.allOf() to fan out 5+ queries in
parallel, collapsing multi-second dashboard load times down to sub-100ms!
Opens autonomous TX2 that commits/rollbacks independently.
If failure must rollback main DB, execute synchronously in TX1.
